subcategory_description: Means-tested payments for people who are out of work or on a low income.
subject_intro: How much Universal Credit pays each month, the extra amounts for children, disability and caring, and how earnings and savings reduce it.
subject_meta_title: Universal Credit Rates 2026/27: Standard Allowance and Extra Amounts
subject_meta_description: Universal Credit for 2026/27: monthly standard allowance from £338.58 to £666.97, child and disability amounts, the 55% taper and work allowances.
label: Standard allowance: single, under 25 (monthly)
context: Every household gets one standard allowance, and the amount depends on age and whether you claim as a single person or a couple.

label: Standard allowance: single, 25 or over (monthly)
context: The standard allowance for a single claimant aged 25 or over.

label: Standard allowance: couple, both under 25 (monthly)
context: One payment for both partners when they both claim.

label: Standard allowance: couple, either 25 or over (monthly)
context: One payment for both partners when at least one of them is 25 or over.

label: Child element for each child (monthly)
context: Paid for every child who lives with you, until the 31 August after their 16th birthday, or their 19th if they're in eligible education.

label: Extra for a first child born before 6 April 2017 (monthly)
context: Added to the child element for your first child, which makes £351.88 in total for that child.

label: Disabled child, lower amount (monthly)
context: For a child who gets any rate of Disability Living Allowance for children or PIP other than the highest.

label: Disabled child, higher amount (monthly)
context: For a child who gets the highest rate of the DLA care component or the higher rate of the PIP daily living part, or who is blind.

label: Share of childcare costs you can claim back
context: For working parents using a registered childcare provider. You pay the costs up front and claim the money back.

label: Most you can claim for childcare, one child (monthly)
context: The monthly cap for one child.

label: Most you can claim for childcare, two or more children (monthly)
context: The monthly cap for two or more children.

label: Health condition element, severe (monthly)
context: For a severe condition that's unlikely to change, or if you're nearing the end of your life. Different rules apply if you reported a condition before 6 April 2026.

label: Health condition element, less severe (monthly)
context: For a condition assessed as less severe or one that may improve over time.

label: Carer element (monthly)
context: For caring at least 35 hours a week for someone who gets a qualifying disability benefit. You can't get it with the higher health element.

label: Taper rate on earnings
context: Your payment goes down by 55p for every £1 you earn after any work allowance.

label: Work allowance with help for housing costs (monthly)
context: You can earn this much before your payment starts to reduce, if you have children or a health condition and get help with housing.

label: Work allowance without help for housing costs (monthly)
context: The higher work allowance, for people with children or a health condition who don't get help with housing costs.

label: Savings you can have before your payment is reduced
context: Above this your payment goes down by £4.35 for every £250 of savings, up to the upper limit.

label: Savings above which you can't usually get it
context: If you have more than this in money, savings and investments you normally can't get Universal Credit.

subcategory_description: Benefits for disabled people and the people who care for them.
subject_intro: How much Carer's Allowance pays, how much you can earn and still get it, and how it affects the State Pension and Universal Credit.
subject_meta_title: Carer's Allowance 2026/27: £86.45 a Week and £204 Earnings Limit
subject_meta_description: Carer's Allowance is £86.45 a week for 2026/27 if you care for someone at least 35 hours a week and earn £204 or less after tax and expenses.
label: Carer's Allowance (weekly)
context: For caring at least 35 hours a week for someone who gets a qualifying disability benefit. In Scotland you apply for Carer Support Payment instead.

label: Most you can earn each week (after tax, NI and expenses)
context: It's a cliff edge, not a taper. Earn more than this in a week and you get no Carer's Allowance for that week.

label: Hours of care needed each week
context: You don't have to live with the person you care for or be related to them.
If you claim Universal Credit, you may get this extra amount for caring, and Carer's Allowance counts as income against it.
Pensioners who get Pension Credit can get this addition if they get Carer's Allowance or have claimed it.

subcategory_description: Benefits for disabled people and the people who care for them.
subject_intro: The weekly rates of Personal Independence Payment for people under State Pension age and Attendance Allowance for those at or over it.
subject_meta_description: Weekly rates for 2026/27: PIP daily living £76.70 or £114.60, PIP mobility £30.30 or £80, and Attendance Allowance £76.70 or £114.60.
label: PIP daily living, lower rate (weekly)
context: Paid if you have a long-term health condition or disability that makes everyday tasks difficult. It's tax-free and not affected by income or savings.

label: PIP daily living, higher rate (weekly)
context: The higher rate of the daily living part.

label: PIP mobility, lower rate (weekly)
context: For people who have difficulty getting around. The higher rate may qualify you for a Motability vehicle.

label: PIP mobility, higher rate (weekly)
context: The higher rate of the mobility part.

label: Attendance Allowance, lower rate (weekly)
context: For people at or over State Pension age who need help looking after themselves. It doesn't cover mobility needs. In Scotland it's Pension Age Disability Payment.

label: Attendance Allowance, higher rate (weekly)
context: The higher rate, for people who need more care.

subcategory_description: Minimum wage, statutory pay, redundancy pay and holiday entitlement.
subject_intro: How statutory redundancy pay is worked out, the cap on a week's pay, and the most anyone can get.
subject_meta_title: Statutory Redundancy Pay 2026/27: £751 Weekly Cap, Maximum £22,530
subject_meta_description: Statutory redundancy pay for 2026/27: half, one or one and a half weeks' pay per year of service, a £751 weekly cap and a £22,530 maximum.
label: Cap on a week's pay
context: Your weekly pay is the average over the 12 weeks before your redundancy notice, and anything above this cap is ignored.

label: Most statutory redundancy pay you can get
context: That's 20 years of service at 1.5 weeks' pay each, at the weekly cap. Your employer can offer more.

label: Most years of service counted
context: Only your most recent 20 years with the employer count.

label: Service needed to qualify
context: You're only entitled to statutory redundancy pay if you've worked for your employer for at least this long.

label: Weeks' pay per full year of service, under 22
context: For each full year you were under 22.

label: Weeks' pay per full year of service, aged 22 to 40
context: For each full year you were 22 or older but under 41.

label: Weeks' pay per full year of service, aged 41 or over
context: For each full year you were 41 or older.

subject_intro: How much paid holiday workers are legally entitled to, and the 28-day limit on the statutory minimum.
subject_meta_title: Statutory Holiday Entitlement: 5.6 Weeks and the 28-Day Limit
subject_meta_description: Workers are legally entitled to 5.6 weeks' paid holiday a year, which is 28 days on a five-day week. Statutory holiday is capped at 28 days.
label: Paid holiday a year
context: Almost all workers get this, including agency workers and people on irregular hours. Part-timers get 5.6 times their usual working week.

label: Most statutory holiday days a year
context: Someone working a five-day week gets 28 days, and someone working six days a week is still limited to 28. Bank holidays can count towards it.

label: Accommodation offset (daily)
context: If an employer provides accommodation free, this is added to the worker's pay for minimum wage purposes. Charges above it reduce their pay.

label: Accommodation offset (weekly)
context: The weekly equivalent of the daily offset.

label: Statutory Adoption Pay (weekly)
context: Paid after the first 6 weeks, which are at 90% of average weekly earnings. It's £194.32 or 90% of earnings, whichever is lower.

label: Statutory Adoption Pay: longest it's paid
context: The first 6 weeks at 90% of earnings, then 33 weeks at the weekly rate.

label: Statutory Shared Parental Pay (weekly)
context: £194.32 or 90% of average weekly earnings, whichever is lower.

label: Plan 1: written off after
context: From the April you were first due to repay, for a first loan paid on or after 1 September 2006. Earlier loans are written off at 65.

label: Plan 2: written off after
context: From the April you were first due to repay.

label: Plan 4: written off after
context: From the April you were first due to repay, for a first loan paid on or after 1 August 2007. Earlier loans are written off at 65 or after 30 years, whichever is first.

label: Plan 5: written off after
context: From the April you were first due to repay.

label: Postgraduate Loan: written off after
context: From the April you were first due to repay, for students from England or Wales.

subcategory_description: Payroll costs and levies that employers pay on top of wages.
subject_intro: The payroll taxes and levies employers pay on top of wages: employer National Insurance, Class 1A, the Apprenticeship Levy, and how much statutory pay they can recover.
subject_meta_title: Employer Payroll Costs 2026/27: NI, Apprenticeship Levy and Statutory Pay Recovery
subject_meta_description: Employer costs for 2026/27: employer National Insurance, 15% Class 1A, the 0.5% Apprenticeship Levy, Employment Allowance and statutory payments recovery.
context: The rate of employer National Insurance on pay above the secondary threshold.
Employers pay National Insurance on each employee's pay above this.
Eligible employers can take this off their yearly employer National Insurance bill.

label: Class 1A National Insurance rate
context: Paid by employers on work benefits such as company cars and phones, and on termination awards over £30,000.

label: Apprenticeship Levy rate
context: Charged on your annual pay bill by employers with a pay bill of more than £3 million.

label: Apprenticeship Levy allowance
context: Reduces the levy you pay each year, for employers who aren't connected to another company or charity.

label: Annual pay bill at which the levy applies
context: Employers and connected companies with a total pay bill above this are liable for the Apprenticeship Levy.

label: Share of statutory pay you can recover (standard)
context: For Statutory Maternity, Paternity, Adoption, Shared Parental, Parental Bereavement and Neonatal Care Pay, if your Class 1 NI bill was over £45,000 last year.

label: Share of statutory pay you can recover (small employer)
context: If your total Class 1 National Insurance for the previous tax year was £45,000 or lower. You cannot recover Statutory Sick Pay.

subcategory_description: Tax-free rates employers can pay for work-related costs.
subject_intro: The tax-free amounts employers can pay for business journeys in your own car, motorcycle or bicycle.
subject_meta_title: Approved Mileage Allowance Rates 2026/27: 55p a Mile for Cars
subject_meta_description: HMRC approved mileage rates for 2026/27: 55p a mile for the first 10,000 business miles in a car, then 25p, 24p for motorcycles and 20p for bicycles.
label: Car or van: first 10,000 business miles (tax)
context: The tax-free rate for using your own car on business journeys, for the first 10,000 miles in a tax year. HMRC raised it from 45p during 2026.

label: Car or van: each mile after 10,000 (tax)
context: For tax purposes the rate drops to this after 10,000 business miles in a tax year. For National Insurance purposes it stays at 55p.

label: Motorcycle (all business miles)
context: The same rate for tax and National Insurance, however many miles.

label: Bicycle (all business miles)
context: The same rate for tax and National Insurance, however many miles.
